title: 1959 AHSME Problem 36
statement: The base of a triangle is \(80,\) and one of the base angles is \(60^\circ.\) The sum of the lengths of the other two sides is \(90.\) The shortest side is:

solutions.text:
Let the side adjacent to the \(60^\circ\) base angle be \(x,\) and let the opposite side be \(90-x.\) The law of cosines gives \[ \begin{aligned} (90-x)^2 &=80^2+x^2\\ &\quad{}-2(80)(x)\cos60^\circ. \end{aligned} \] Simplifying yields \(8100-180x=6400-80x,\) so \(x=17.\) The side lengths are \(17,\ 73,\) and \(80,\) and the shortest is \(17.\)

Thus, the correct answer is D.
hints: Let the side adjacent to the \(60^\circ\) angle be \(x\), so the third side is \(90-x\)
Apply the law of cosines with included sides \(80\) and \(x\)
